name: The Hub: Founding Day — Sole Trader, Partnership or Limited Company
description: A 60-minute legal-form decision lab for IB Business Management Year 12. Three Year-12 students must register The Hub, their student-run snack bar, before they can open. Across three rounds — Discover, Stress-Test, Choose & Defend — participants weigh six axes (liability, control, capital, continuity, set-up cost, profit distribution) across five forms (sole trader, partnership, private limited company, cooperative, social enterprise). The aha moment: there is no objectively right answer. The right form depends on which axis matters most, and that depends on the founders goals.

Your Decisions

The school librarian printout lists five legal forms. There are not three forms — there are six axes of trade-off (liability, control, capital, continuity, set-up cost, profit distribution). For each founder, pick the axis that matters most to them.

M
Maya

Maya — the operator. Wants the doors open in four weeks. Will run service, ordering and the till.

D
Daniel

Daniel — the investor. Put in €2,000 of the €4,000. Worried about getting his money back.

A
Aisha

Aisha — the cautious one. Has a part-time tutoring offer. Wants a bounded downside.

Three what-if futures. For each scenario, pick the form that handles it best. Remember: the form you pick is chosen by the worst day you are willing to imagine.

Scenario A — The Bad Week

Three months in, the bakery delivers €3,000 of stock that sits unsold. The Hub owes €3,000 and has €400 in the bank. Final-demand letter arrives. Who pays the missing €2,600?

Scenario B — The Friendship Break

After one year, Aisha takes the tutoring job and wants out. She wants her €800 back. Maya and Daniel want to continue. Which form makes this clean?

Scenario C — The Wild Success

After one year, the parent association offers €15,000 for a stake to fund a permanent fit-out and second location. Which form lets The Hub take the money cleanly?

Pick one form for The Hub. Name the axis you are weighting most heavily. The advisory committee will then surface the strongest counter-argument from the rejected forms.
